classification.difficultyReason: Read increasing or decreasing behaviour and concavity directly from five supplied curves.

content.prompt: For each curve, identify the sign of $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ and $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$.

spec.description: Unticked axes with arrows at both ends; increasing concave-up curve has a negative y-intercept and positive x-intercept. The equation used to construct the qualitative curve is not a supplied given.
spec.mathematics: Positive gradient and positive second derivative throughout the displayed curve.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied curve only; derivative signs appear only in answers.

answer.worked: The curve is increasing, so $\dfrac{dy}{dx}>0$. Its gradient increases as $x$ increases, so it is concave up and $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}>0$.

spec.description: Unticked axes with arrows at both ends; decreasing concave-down curve has positive y- and x-intercepts. The construction equation is not a supplied given.
spec.mathematics: Negative gradient and negative second derivative throughout the displayed curve.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied curve only; derivative signs appear only in answers.

answer.worked: The curve is decreasing, so $\dfrac{dy}{dx}<0$. Its gradient becomes more negative as $x$ increases, so it is concave down and $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}<0$.

spec.description: Unticked axes with arrows at both ends; first-quadrant increasing curve becomes flatter to the right, with arrows at both curve ends. The construction equation is not a supplied given.
spec.mathematics: Positive gradient and negative second derivative.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied curve only; derivative signs appear only in answers.

answer.worked: The curve is increasing, so $\dfrac{dy}{dx}>0$. Its positive gradient decreases as $x$ increases, so it is concave down and $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}<0$.

answer.worked: The curve is decreasing, so $\dfrac{dy}{dx}<0$. Its gradient becomes less negative as $x$ increases, so it is concave up and $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}>0$.
